title: Process Automation, Logic, and Integration
summary: Make Salesforce do the work: triggers that scale, async jobs that recover, and integrations that don't break.

lessons.title: Order of Execution & Recursion
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, apply trigger best practices, including order of execution and recursion control, alongside declarative automation.

cards.title: The save pipeline (simplified)
items: Commit, then post-commit work (emails, async jobs)

cards.body: **Flow before Trigger, Validate after.** Before-save flows run first, then before triggers, THEN your validation rules check the result.

cards.title: Free field updates
cards.body: Changing fields on **Trigger.new in a before trigger** needs no DML. Updating the same record in an after trigger needs extra DML and re-fires triggers.

cards.title: Workflow re-fire
cards.body: A **workflow field update** saves the record again and runs **before update + after update triggers one more time**. Custom validation rules do not run again.
A **static Boolean** 'already ran' flag breaks bulk loads: triggers run in chunks of **200** in the SAME transaction, so chunk 2 sees the flag and is skipped.

cards.title: Safer recursion guard
cards.body: Set.add() returns false if the Id is already there. Per-record, not per-transaction.

lessons.title: Bulk-Safe Trigger Frameworks
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, apply trigger best practices and Apex error handling for bulk-safe, maintainable logic.

cards.title: Framework rules
items: Trigger is thin: delegate to a **handler class**

cards.title: Why one trigger?
cards.body: With several triggers on one object for the same event, **execution order is not guaranteed**. One trigger + handler = you control the order.

cards.title: Thin trigger
cards.body: All logic lives in testable Apex classes.

cards.title: Block one bad record
cards.body: addError marks just that record (or field) as failed. The user sees the message.

cards.title: Custom exceptions
cards.body: Extend **Exception** and the class name **must end in 'Exception'**: public class PaymentException extends Exception {}
With **allOrNone = true** (plain DML), one addError fails the whole batch. With **Database.insert(list, false)**, only flagged records fail.

lessons.title: Future vs Queueable
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, implement asynchronous Apex using future methods and Queueable Apex, including chaining.

cards.title: @future
cards.body: Static, void, **primitives or collections of primitives only**. No sObjects.

cards.title: Queueable
cards.body: Takes **sObjects and complex types**, returns a **job Id** you can monitor.

cards.title: Limits to memorize
items: **50** enqueueJob calls in a synchronous transaction
Only **1** child job from an executing Queueable
Chain depth unlimited, except **5** in Developer Edition / trial orgs

cards.title: Delay + control
cards.body: **System.enqueueJob(job, delayMinutes)** delays 0-10 minutes. **AsyncOptions** sets MinimumQueueableDelayInMinutes, MaximumQueueableStackDepth and a **DuplicateSignature** to block duplicate jobs.
You **cannot call a future method from a future or batch** context. Check System.isFuture() / System.isBatch() before calling.
**Future = Fire-and-Forget. Queueable = Queue it, Track it, Chain it.**

lessons.title: Transaction Finalizers
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, implement asynchronous Apex with error recovery using Transaction Finalizers.

cards.title: The problem
cards.body: A Queueable hits an **uncaught exception** or limit. Its DML rolls back, and a try/catch can't catch limit exceptions. How do you log it or retry?

cards.title: Attach a finalizer
cards.body: Runs after the Queueable finishes, success OR failure.

cards.title: Rules
items: Runs in its **own transaction** with fresh limits
Can enqueue **one** async job; callouts allowed
A failing Queueable can be re-enqueued **5** consecutive times

cards.body: **Finalizer = the cleanup crew.** It shows up after the party, even if the party crashed.

lessons.title: Batch Apex & Scheduling
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, implement Batch Apex and Schedulable Apex for large data volumes.

cards.title: Batch skeleton
cards.body: Each execute() gets **fresh governor limits**.

cards.title: QueryLocator vs Iterable
items: Iterable: normal SOQL row limit (**50,000**) applies
Iterable: for custom logic or non-SOQL sources

cards.title: Database.Stateful
cards.body: Keeps **instance variables** across execute() calls (counters, error lists). Without it, each chunk starts with a fresh copy. Static variables never carry over.

cards.title: Queue limits
items: **5** batch jobs queued or active at once
Up to **100** more wait in the **Apex flex queue** (Holding)
Chain batches by calling Database.executeBatch in finish()

cards.title: Schedule it
cards.body: Max **100** scheduled Apex jobs per org.
Scheduled Apex **cannot make synchronous callouts**. Start a Queueable or Batch that implements **Database.AllowsCallouts** instead.

lessons.title: Pick the Right Async Tool
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, choose the appropriate asynchronous Apex tool.

cards.title: Decision cheat sheet
items: Simple callout from a trigger: **@future(callout=true)** or Queueable
Need guaranteed cleanup on failure: **Queueable + Finalizer**

cards.title: Triggers + callouts
cards.body: A trigger **can't make a synchronous callout**. The record is mid-transaction. Hand the work to async Apex that allows callouts.

cards.title: Monitoring
cards.body: Batch, Queueable and future jobs all show up in **AsyncApexJob** and the Apex Jobs page. Only Queueable and Batch hand you the job Id directly.
**F-Q-B-S**: Future (fast & simple), Queueable (flexible), Batch (big), Schedule (clock).
Calling Database.executeBatch from a trigger for every save floods the 5-job limit and the flex queue. Batch is for **big bulk work**, not per-record reactions.

lessons.title: Platform Events
lessons.objective: Identify the appropriate publish/subscribe logic for platform events.

cards.title: Publish
cards.body: Event objects end in **__e**. EventBus.publish counts as a DML statement.

cards.title: Publish behavior
items: **Publish After Commit**: sent only if the transaction commits
**Publish Immediately**: sent right away, even if the transaction **rolls back**
Use Immediately for error logging that must survive a rollback

cards.title: Event triggers are different
cards.body: They run as the **Automated Process** user (change it with PlatformEventSubscriberConfig), in batches of up to **2,000** events, asynchronously from the publisher.

cards.title: Resume after failure
cards.body: If the trigger dies, the next run starts after the checkpoint. Or throw **EventBus.RetryableException** to retry (up to 9 times).
Platform events are **not** rolled back by Database.rollback when published immediately. And you can't query or update events like records.

lessons.title: Change Data Capture
lessons.objective: Identify the appropriate publish/subscribe logic for Change Data Capture events.

cards.title: What it is
cards.body: Salesforce **auto-publishes** change events when records are created, updated, deleted or undeleted. You just **select the objects** in Setup. No publishing code.

cards.title: Read the header
cards.body: Header has changeType, recordIds, changedFields, commitUser, entityName.

cards.title: Commit-only
cards.body: Change events are published **after the transaction commits**. Rolled-back changes produce no events. Retained for **3 days** for replay.
**PE = you design the message. CDC = Salesforce writes the diary of record changes.**

lessons.title: Outbound Callouts
lessons.objective: Apply programmatic integration techniques for outbound communication, including callouts, Named Credentials and Continuations.

cards.title: REST callout
cards.body: **callout:** prefix = Named Credential. No Remote Site Setting needed.

cards.title: Callout limits
items: Default timeout **10 s**, max **120 s** per callout
Max **120 s** total callout time per transaction
Body size: **6 MB** sync, **12 MB** async

cards.title: Named + External Credentials
cards.body: **Named Credential** = the URL. **External Credential** = the auth (OAuth, JWT, custom headers) + principals. Users get access to a principal through a **permission set**.
DML **then** callout in one transaction throws **CalloutException: You have uncommitted work pending**. Callout first, or move the callout to async.

cards.title: SOAP
cards.body: Import a WSDL with **WSDL2Apex** (Generate from WSDL) to get typed stub classes. Test with **WebServiceMock**. REST tests use **HttpCalloutMock** via Test.setMock.

cards.title: Continuation
cards.body: For long-running calls from **LWC/Aura/Visualforce**: @AuraEnabled(continuation=true cacheable=true). Up to **3** callouts per Continuation, timeout up to **120 s**, without tying up a server thread.

lessons.title: Inbound: Apex REST & SOAP
lessons.objective: Apply programmatic integration techniques for inbound communication using Apex REST and Apex SOAP web services.

cards.title: Apex REST
cards.body: Endpoint: **/services/apexrest/orders/{id}**

cards.title: Apex REST rules
items: Only **one method per annotation** per class

cards.body: If an @HttpPost method **has parameters**, the JSON body is deserialized into them and **requestBody is not populated**. Need the raw body? Use **no parameters** and read RestContext.request.requestBody.

cards.title: Apex SOAP
cards.body: Use **webservice static**. Generate the WSDL from the class page and give it to the consumer.
**G.S. = Global Static.** Every inbound Apex web method needs both.

lessons.title: Flow Meets Apex
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, choose between declarative automation and Apex, and expose Apex to Flow with invocable actions.

cards.title: Invocable action
cards.body: Flow can now call **Score Leads**.

cards.title: @InvocableMethod rules
items: **One** per class; class must be an outer class
**One** parameter: a List (or List of Lists)

cards.body: Flow **batches interviews**: 200 records can hit your method as **one call with a 200-item list**. SOQL inside a loop over that list = limit error.

cards.title: Flow or trigger?
items: Complex logic, heavy data, callouts in bulk: **Apex**

cards.body: **One door, one list in, one list out.** That's an invocable method.

lessons.title: Database Methods & Safe SOQL
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, use Database class methods, handle mixed DML, and write secure dynamic SOQL.

cards.title: Partial success
cards.body: **allOrNone = false**: good rows save, bad rows report errors.

cards.title: Upsert by external Id
cards.body: Matches on the external Id field. No Salesforce Ids needed.

cards.title: Mixed DML
cards.body: DML on **setup objects** (User, Group, GroupMember, PermissionSetAssignment, UserRole) and normal objects in one transaction throws **MIXED_DML_OPERATION**. Move one side to **@future** or Queueable. In tests, wrap in **System.runAs**.
String concatenation of user input into Database.query = **SOQL injection**. Use bind variables, Database.queryWithBinds, or String.escapeSingleQuotes.

cards.title: Safe dynamic SOQL
cards.body: Field and object names **can't be bound**: whitelist them against Schema describe results.

cards.title: Undo button
cards.body: **Savepoint sp = Database.setSavepoint();** ... **Database.rollback(sp);** rolls back DML since the savepoint. Each counts against DML limits.

flashcards.back: The record is saved again: before update and after update triggers run one more time. Custom validation rules do not run again.
Triggers process up to 200 records per chunk. Bigger DML runs the trigger several times in the same transaction.

questions.q: An admin builds a before-save record-triggered flow on Case that sets Priority. A developer's before insert trigger on Case reads Priority to set an SLA date. In what order do they run?
options: The before trigger runs first, so it always sees the original Priority
The before-save flow runs first, so the trigger sees the Priority the flow set
They run in parallel, so the order cannot be predicted
The flow runs after the after insert trigger, so the trigger never sees its value
questions.explain: Before-save record-triggered flows run before before triggers. The trigger sees the value the flow set.
wrong: Before triggers run after before-save flows.
Salesforce runs these steps one after another, in a documented order.
That describes after-save flows, not before-save flows.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Triggers and Order of Execution

questions.q: An after update trigger on Account updates related records. A workflow field update made the trigger fire twice, so the developer added a static Boolean 'hasRun' flag. Now a Data Loader update of 600 Accounts only processes the first 200. What is the best fix?
options: Reset hasRun to false at the end of the before update trigger
Set the Data Loader batch size to 600 so all records arrive in one chunk
Replace the Boolean with a static Set<Id> and skip only records whose Ids are already in the set
Move the logic to a before update trigger, which only fires once per transaction
questions.explain: Triggers process 200 records per chunk inside one transaction, so a static Boolean blocks chunks 2 and 3. A static Set<Id> guards each record without skipping new ones.
wrong: This runs before the workflow update and gets complicated fast. The flag would still be shared across chunks.
Triggers still get records in chunks of 200, whatever the API batch size.
Workflow field updates fire before update triggers again too.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Triggers and Order of Execution; Bulk Triggers

questions.q: Which two steps run AFTER the after triggers in the save order of execution? (Choose 2)
options: Assignment rules
Before-save record-triggered flows
Custom validation rules
Roll-up summary calculation on the parent record
Duplicate rules
questions.explain: After triggers are followed by assignment, auto-response and workflow rules, after-save flows, and then roll-up summary updates on parents.
wrong: These run before before triggers.
These run after before triggers and before the record is saved.
Duplicate rules run before the record is saved, before after triggers.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Triggers and Order of Execution

questions.q: A developer must set Region__c on Lead based on the Lead's State whenever a Lead is created. Which approach uses the fewest resources?
options: An after insert trigger that queries the Leads and calls update
A Queueable job enqueued from an after insert trigger
A scheduled job that fixes Region__c every hour
A before insert trigger that sets Region__c on the records in Trigger.new
questions.explain: In a before trigger, changes to Trigger.new are saved with no extra DML or query.
wrong: Needs extra SOQL and DML, and re-fires update triggers.
Async adds delay and a second transaction for a simple same-record change.
Leaves data wrong for up to an hour and wastes resources.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Trigger Context Variables

questions.q: A team has three before update triggers on Opportunity written by different developers. Behaviour changes unpredictably between releases. What should the architect recommend?
options: Merge into one trigger per object that delegates to a handler class controlling the order of logic
Add a Trigger Order setting in Setup to rank the triggers
Convert all three triggers to after update triggers
Put each trigger's logic in a separate @future method
questions.explain: Salesforce does not guarantee the order of multiple triggers for the same object and event. One trigger with a handler gives you full control.
wrong: There is no Setup option to order Apex triggers.
Order is still not guaranteed, and same-record updates get more expensive.
Adds async complexity and doesn't fix ordering.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Triggers; Trailhead: Apex Triggers best practices

questions.q: A nightly integration inserts 1,000 Contacts with Database.insert(contacts, false). A before insert trigger calls addError() on 3 records with invalid emails. What happens?
options: All 1,000 records are rolled back and a DmlException is thrown
The 3 records are saved but flagged with a warning
997 records are saved; the 3 records fail and their errors appear in the SaveResults
The trigger skips the 3 records and saves them without the email field
questions.explain: With allOrNone set to false, records marked with addError fail on their own and the rest commit. Each failure shows up in its SaveResult.
wrong: That would happen with plain insert DML or allOrNone = true.
addError blocks the save. It is not a warning.
addError does not strip fields. It fails the record.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: SObject addError; Database.SaveResult

questions.q: This trigger works in testing but fails with 'Too many SOQL queries: 101' during a 200-record data load. What is the best refactor?
options: Wrap the query in a try/catch so the LimitException is handled
Collect the AccountIds into a Set, query once into a Map<Id, Account>, then loop and look up each Account
Move the query into an @future method called once per Case
Add LIMIT 1 to the query so each query costs less
questions.explain: Bulkify: one query for all parent Accounts, then look them up from a Map inside the loop. That uses 1 SOQL query no matter how many records there are.
wrong: LimitException can't be caught.
Before triggers can't change records from async code, and 200 future calls exceed the limit of 50.
LIMIT doesn't reduce the number of queries.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Bulk Apex Triggers; Execution Governors and Limits

questions.q: A developer wants a custom exception to throw when a payment fails. Which declaration compiles?
options: public class PaymentError extends Exception {}
public class PaymentException implements Exception {}
public exception PaymentException {}
public class PaymentException extends Exception {}
questions.explain: Custom exceptions extend Exception, and their names must end with 'Exception'.
wrong: The name must end with 'Exception'.
Exception is a class to extend, not an interface.
There is no 'exception' type keyword in Apex.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Create Custom Exceptions

questions.q: A developer must pass a List<Opportunity> with in-memory changes to asynchronous code. Which option supports this?
options: An @future method with a List<Opportunity> parameter
An @future method with a Map<Id, Opportunity> parameter
A class that implements Queueable and stores the list in a member variable
A Schedulable class that takes the list in its execute method
questions.explain: Queueable jobs can hold sObjects and other complex types as member variables. Future methods only accept primitives or collections of primitives.
wrong: Future methods can't take sObjects.
Maps of sObjects aren't allowed either.
Schedulable.execute only takes a SchedulableContext.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Future Methods; Queueable Apex

questions.q: Inside an executing Queueable job, a developer calls System.enqueueJob() in a loop to start 3 follow-up jobs. What happens?
options: The first call succeeds and the second throws a LimitException, because an executing Queueable can only enqueue one child job
All three jobs run in parallel
All three jobs run in order, one after another
The calls are ignored until the parent job commits, then only the last one runs
questions.explain: An executing Queueable can add only one job to the queue. To run more work, chain: each job enqueues the next.
wrong: The second enqueue fails.
Only one child is allowed. Sequence work by chaining instead.
The limit throws an exception. Calls aren't silently ignored.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Queueable Apex (Chaining Jobs); Execution Governors and Limits

questions.q: A Queueable must call an external API, wait at least 5 minutes before it starts (to let the remote system catch up), and not be enqueued twice for the same record. Which two actions should the developer take? (Choose 2)
options: Use @future(callout=true, delay=5)
Have the Queueable class implement Database.AllowsCallouts
Enqueue with AsyncOptions, setting MinimumQueueableDelayInMinutes to 5 and a DuplicateSignature built from the record Id
Call a busy-wait loop for 5 minutes at the start of execute()
Schedule a Schedulable class for 5 minutes from now with a callout in its execute method
questions.explain: Database.AllowsCallouts lets a Queueable make callouts. AsyncOptions supports a minimum delay and a duplicate signature that stops a second identical job being enqueued.
wrong: @future has no delay attribute.
Burns CPU time and would hit limits.
Scheduled Apex can't make synchronous callouts.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Queueable Apex; AsyncOptions Class

questions.q: An Account trigger calls an @future method to sync data. A new Batch Apex job updates Accounts and fails with 'Future method cannot be called from a future or batch method'. What is the best fix?
options: Add Database.Stateful to the batch class
Lower the batch scope to 1 record
Add @future to the batch execute method
In the trigger handler, check System.isBatch() and System.isFuture(), and enqueue a Queueable or skip the call in those contexts
questions.explain: Future methods can't be called from batch or future contexts. Detect the context and use another path, such as a Queueable.
wrong: State has nothing to do with this error.
The context is still batch, whatever the scope.
Batch interface methods can't be future methods.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Future Methods; System Class

questions.q: A Queueable job sometimes fails with an uncatchable limit exception. Its DML is rolled back, but the team still needs a log record saying which job failed. What should the developer use?
options: A try/catch block around the whole execute method
A class implementing Finalizer, attached with System.attachFinalizer() inside execute()
A Database.Stateful variable that stores the error
A Savepoint created at the start of execute()
questions.explain: A Transaction Finalizer runs in its own transaction after the Queueable finishes, even when it fails. It can read the exception and save a log.
wrong: Limit exceptions can't be caught.
Database.Stateful is for Batch Apex. The state would be lost on failure anyway.
Savepoints don't survive an uncaught exception, and the log needs its own transaction.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Transaction Finalizers

questions.q: A Finalizer re-enqueues its Queueable whenever the result is UNHANDLED_EXCEPTION. The external system is down for an hour, so every attempt fails. What does the platform do?
options: It retries forever until the job succeeds
It blocks the first re-enqueue, because finalizers can't enqueue jobs
It allows up to 5 consecutive re-enqueues of the failing job, then stops
It suspends all Queueable jobs in the org for 24 hours
questions.explain: A Queueable that fails with an unhandled exception can be re-enqueued by its finalizer up to 5 consecutive times. Build in your own retry count and alerting.
wrong: There is a limit on consecutive failed re-enqueues.
Finalizers can enqueue one async job.
There is no such org-wide suspension.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Transaction Finalizers (Limits)

questions.q: How many Transaction Finalizers can be attached to one Queueable job?
options: One
Two: one for success and one for failure
Up to 5
Up to 50
questions.explain: Only one finalizer can be attached per Queueable. It checks getResult() for both success and failure.
wrong: A single finalizer handles both outcomes.
Only one is allowed.
Only one is allowed.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Transaction Finalizers

questions.q: A Batch Apex job must email a summary of how many records failed across all chunks. The count is always 0 in finish(). What should the developer change?
options: Make the counter a static variable
Increase the batch scope to 2,000
Write the counter to a Custom Label
Implement Database.Stateful and keep the counter as an instance variable
questions.explain: Database.Stateful keeps instance variables across execute() transactions, so the counter survives into finish().
wrong: Static variables reset in each batch transaction.
More chunks would still lose the count, and it doesn't fix state.
Custom Labels can't be updated from Apex at run time.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Using State in Batch Apex

questions.q: A batch must process about 8 million Task records selected by a simple SOQL filter. What should start() return?
options: An Iterable<Task> built from a SOQL query
A Database.QueryLocator
A List<Task> from a SOQL query
A Database.Cursor holding the query
questions.explain: A QueryLocator can retrieve up to 50 million records. An Iterable is subject to the normal SOQL row limit of 50,000.
wrong: Iterable start methods are bound by the 50,000 query row limit.
A List is an Iterable and hits the same row limit.
Batch start() supports QueryLocator or Iterable, not a cursor.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Using Batch Apex

questions.q: Every night at 1 AM an org must send updated prices to an ERP REST API. Which two designs work? (Choose 2)
options: A Schedulable class whose execute() makes the HTTP callout directly
A Schedulable class that starts a Batch Apex job implementing Database.AllowsCallouts
A Schedulable class that enqueues a Queueable implementing Database.AllowsCallouts
Set callout=true on the Schedulable class's execute method
An after update trigger on Pricebook entries that waits until 1 AM
questions.explain: Scheduled Apex can't make synchronous callouts. It must hand off to async Apex that allows callouts, such as a Batch or Queueable.
wrong: Synchronous callouts aren't supported in scheduled Apex.
There is no callout attribute for Schedulable.
Triggers can't wait for a time of day.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Apex Scheduler

questions.q: Which cron expression runs a scheduled Apex job every day at 2:00 AM?
questions.explain: Apex cron fields are Seconds Minutes Hours Day_of_month Month Day_of_week [Year]. '0 0 2 * * ?' is 02:00:00 every day.
wrong: This is 5-field Unix cron. Apex needs seconds first.
This means 00:00:02, two seconds after midnight.
Hours use a 24-hour clock, so 14 means 2:00 PM.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Apex Scheduler (cron expressions)

questions.q: A developer needs async processing that takes a list of sObjects as input, returns a job Id to show progress in the UI, and can start a follow-up job when done. Which tool fits best?
options: @future method
Schedulable Apex
Queueable Apex
A platform event
questions.explain: Queueable accepts sObjects, returns a job Id from System.enqueueJob, and supports chaining.
wrong: No sObject params, no job Id returned, no chaining.
Built for time-based runs, not on-demand processing with sObject input.
Events decouple systems but don't give you a job Id for this work.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Queueable Apex

questions.q: Every Sunday an org must recalculate a score on 3 million Contact records. Which solution is most appropriate?
options: A Queueable that loops through all Contacts in one execute()
An @future method called once a week by a user
A record-triggered flow on Contact
A Batch Apex class started by a Schedulable class
questions.explain: Batch Apex splits millions of records into chunks with fresh limits, and Schedulable runs it weekly.
wrong: One transaction can't query or update 3 million rows.
Future has the same single-transaction limits, and it isn't scheduled.

WHERE WhatId != null GROUP BY TYPEOF What

questions.explain: Filter on a polymorphic field with the Type qualifier, or with a reference-field semi-join that limits WhatId to Account Ids.
wrong: TYPEOF is only allowed in the SELECT clause.
instanceof is an Apex operator, not SOQL.
TYPEOF can't be used with GROUP BY, and grouping doesn't filter by type anyway.
questions.source: SOQL and SOSL Reference: TYPEOF; Comparison Operators

questions.q: A service lead asks for every Case created 'in the last 7 days', and wants to know whether today's Cases are included. Which records does this query return?
options: Cases from the 7 full days before today; today's Cases are excluded
Cases created from 12:00 AM seven days before today up to now, so today is included (8 calendar days)
Cases created in the last 168 hours, counted from the current time
None: date literals can't be compared to DateTime fields with =
questions.explain: LAST_N_DAYS:n starts at 12:00 AM n days before the current day and runs up to the current second, so it includes today. LAST_N_DAYS:1 means yesterday and today.
wrong: LAST_N_DAYS includes today; LAST_N_DAYS:1 means yesterday and today.
Date literals start at midnight in the user's locale, not at the current time minus a number of hours.
Using = with a date literal on a DateTime field matches the whole range; that's the normal syntax.
questions.source: SOQL and SOSL Reference: Date Formats and Date Literals in WHERE

questions.q: A reusable selector builds this query at run time. It fails with 'Variable does not exist: acct.Id'. Which two changes fix it? (Choose 2)
options: Assign the value to a local variable first (Id acctId = acct.Id;) and bind :acctId in the string
Concatenate the sObject into the string: '... WHERE AccountId = \'' + acct + '\''
Use Database.queryWithBinds with ':acctId' in the string and a Map such as {'acctId' => acct.Id}
Declare the acct parameter as final so Database.query can see its fields
Change the bind to :acct.get('Id')
questions.explain: Unlike inline SOQL, Database.query only supports simple bind variables, not fields such as acct.Id. Resolve the field into a local variable, or pass the value in the bind map of Database.queryWithBinds.
wrong: Concatenating the sObject inserts its whole string form, not its Id, and opens the door to SOQL injection.
final doesn't change how bind variables are resolved.
Method calls in bind expressions aren't supported in dynamic SOQL strings.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Dynamic SOQL

questions.q: A pipeline filter builds its bind map from user choices. A bug adds a second key. What happens when this runs?
options: It returns Qualification Opportunities, because the last value put wins
It returns Prospecting Opportunities, because the key 'stage' matches the bind name exactly
A QueryException is thrown, because the bind map has keys that differ only in case
It doesn't compile, because Map<String, Object> can't hold an Integer value
questions.explain: queryWithBinds compares map keys case-insensitively and throws a QueryException when keys differ only in case ('The bindMap consists of duplicate case-insensitive keys').
wrong: Both keys stay in the map (String keys are case-sensitive), so there's no 'last one wins'.
Bind name matching in queryWithBinds is case-insensitive, so both keys match and conflict.
Map<String, Object> holds any value type, including Integer.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Dynamic SOQL

questions.q: A generic export utility reads values from queried records by field path. What happens on the last line, and what is the fix?
options: It throws an SObjectException (invalid field); read the parent first: rec.getSObject('Account').get('Name')
It returns the Account name, because get() follows relationship paths
It returns null, because parent fields must be read with get('Account__r.Name')
It throws a TypeException on the cast; use String.valueOf(rec.get('Account.Name'))
questions.explain: get() takes a field on the sObject itself. A parent field is reached with getSObject('Account') to get the parent record, then get('Name') on it.
wrong: get() doesn't follow dot paths.
Account is a standard lookup, so its relationship name is Account, and get() still can't follow paths.
The error is the invalid field name, not the cast.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Dynamic DML

questions.q: A generic CSV export receives an object name and a list of field names from a Lightning page. It must keep only the fields that exist and that the running user can read. What goes in the if condition?
options: tok.getDescribe().isUpdateable()
fieldMap.containsKey(f)
tok != null && tok.getDescribe().isPermissionable()
tok != null && tok.getDescribe().isAccessible()
questions.explain: DescribeFieldResult.isAccessible() is true when the running user can see the field. Checking for null first skips names that aren't fields on the object.
wrong: isUpdateable() checks edit access, which is stricter than read and would drop read-only fields; it also fails on a null token.
containsKey only proves the field exists, not that the user can read it.
isPermissionable() says whether field permissions can be set on the field, not whether this user has them.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Understanding Apex Describe Information

questions.q: Tax rules differ by region, so the org stores each region's handler class name in Custom Metadata (for example, 'EmeaTaxHandler'). Every handler implements the TaxHandler interface. Which line creates the right handler at run time?
options: TaxHandler h = new Type(cfg.Handler_Class__c);
TaxHandler h = (TaxHandler) Type.forName(cfg.Handler_Class__c).newInstance();
TaxHandler h = (TaxHandler) Schema.getGlobalDescribe().get(cfg.Handler_Class__c).newSObject();
TaxHandler h = Type.forName(cfg.Handler_Class__c);
questions.explain: Type.forName returns the System.Type for a class name, newInstance() creates an object of it, and the cast to the interface lets the code call it.
wrong: Type has no public constructor that takes a class name.
getGlobalDescribe() describes sObjects, not Apex classes.
Type.forName returns a Type, not an instance; you still need newInstance() and a cast.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: Type Class

questions.q: A validation rule on Opportunity blocks saving when Discount__c > 30 and Approved__c is false. A before update trigger raises the discount for Strategic accounts. A rep edits the Next Step on a Strategic Opportunity (Approved__c is false) in the UI. What happens?
options: The save succeeds, because validation rules run before before triggers and only see the rep's input
The save succeeds, because validation rules don't evaluate field values set by Apex
The save is blocked by the validation rule, because custom validation rules run after before triggers and see the trigger's value
The save succeeds, and the validation rule blocks the record later when a workflow rule re-runs validation
questions.explain: Before triggers run first, then system validation runs again with custom validation rules. The rule sees Discount__c = 35 and blocks the save.
wrong: Custom validation rules run after before triggers, not before them.
Validation rules check the final values, including those set by before triggers.
Custom validation rules aren't re-run after workflow field updates, and here the save is already blocked.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Triggers and Order of Execution

questions.q: Touches__c on a Lead is 1. A user changes it to 10. A workflow rule field update then adds 1, making it 11. The after update trigger below runs again after the workflow field update. What does that second run log?
options: old=1 new=11
old=10 new=11
old=11 new=11
old=1 new=10
questions.explain: In the update trigger that fires after a workflow field update, Trigger.old holds the record as it was before the initial update (1), not the value the user saved (10).
wrong: This is the documented exception: Trigger.old isn't the value right before the workflow update.
Trigger.old never contains the workflow's new value.
Trigger.new in the re-run includes the workflow field update (11).
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Triggers and Order of Execution

questions.q: An org still has a legacy workflow rule with a field update on Case. When it fires during an update, which two things run again for that record? (Choose 2)
options: Custom validation rules
Before update and after update triggers (one more time)
Duplicate rules
System validations
Before-save record-triggered flows
questions.explain: After a workflow field update, the record is updated again, system validations run again, and before and after update triggers fire one more time. Custom validation rules, flows, duplicate rules, processes and escalation rules aren't run again.
wrong: Custom validation rules aren't run again after a workflow field update.
Duplicate rules aren't run again.
Flows aren't run again for a workflow field update.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Triggers and Order of Execution

questions.q: An admin adds an after-save record-triggered flow on Opportunity that updates the triggering record's Next_Review__c field. Since then, reps get two follow-up Tasks when they move a deal to Negotiation. What is happening, and what is the best fix?
options: Record-triggered flows always run in a separate transaction, so the trigger fires once in each; make the flow run asynchronously
The platform always fires after update triggers twice when any flow exists on the object; use a static Boolean to stop the second run
Duplicate rules re-run after the flow and copy the Task; turn off the duplicate rule on Task
The flow's update sends the record through the save procedure again, so the trigger runs twice; create the Task only when StageName changed compared to Trigger.oldMap
questions.explain: When an after-save flow updates the record, it goes through the save procedure again and the update triggers fire again. In that second save, the old stage is already Negotiation, so comparing to Trigger.oldMap stops the duplicate Task.
wrong: The flow runs in the same transaction as the save that triggered it.
Triggers fire again because of the flow's DML, not just because a flow exists; and a static Boolean blocks records in later 200-record chunks.
Duplicate rules don't create records.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Triggers and Order of Execution

questions.q: Invoice_Line__c is the detail in a master-detail with Invoice__c, which has a roll-up summary field Total__c. Invoice__c has an after update trigger that queues an ERP sync. A Data Loader job inserts 500 lines spread across 20 Invoices. What happens to the Invoice trigger?
options: It doesn't fire, because roll-up summaries are calculated after commit
It fires for the 20 Invoices, because recalculating the roll-up summary sends each parent through the save procedure
It doesn't fire, because roll-up summary fields update like formula fields, without a save
It fires only if the Data Loader job uses all-or-none mode
questions.explain: When a child changes a roll-up summary, the platform recalculates it and the parent record goes through the save procedure, so the parent's update triggers run. Check whether Total__c really changed before queueing work.
wrong: Roll-up recalculation happens before commit, inside the same transaction.
Roll-up summaries are stored values; the parent is saved and its triggers fire.
All-or-none mode doesn't decide whether parent triggers fire.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Triggers and Order of Execution

questions.q: On Lead, a before-save flow sets Rating, a before insert trigger lowercases Email, a duplicate rule blocks Leads with a matching Email, and an after insert trigger creates a Task. Which two statements are true for a new Lead? (Choose 2)
options: If the duplicate rule blocks the Lead, the after insert trigger still runs but its Task is rolled back
The duplicate rule runs before custom validation rules
The before insert trigger can only see the Rating value after the Lead is committed
The before-save flow runs before the before insert trigger
The duplicate rule checks the lowercased Email set by the trigger
questions.explain: The order is before-save flows, before triggers, validation (system and custom), then duplicate rules, then save. A blocking duplicate rule stops the save before after triggers run.
wrong: When a duplicate rule blocks, no further steps run, including after triggers.
Duplicate rules run after custom validation rules.
The before-save flow already ran, so the trigger sees Rating in Trigger.new.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Triggers and Order of Execution

questions.q: An integration calls Database.update(accounts, false) on 100 Accounts. Two fail a validation rule. The after update trigger below writes audit rows and uses a static Set to stop recursion. What is the outcome?
options: 98 Accounts are saved with 98 audit rows
98 Accounts are saved with 196 audit rows, because the trigger ran twice
98 Accounts are saved, but no audit rows are saved
The whole update fails with 'Too many batch retries in the presence of Apex triggers and partial failures'
questions.explain: With partial success, the first attempt is rolled back and the trigger runs again on the 98 good records. Static variables aren't reset, so the Set already holds their Ids and the retry skips them; the audit rows from the first attempt were rolled back.
wrong: The retry skips every record because the static Set wasn't reset.
The first attempt's audit rows are rolled back, and the retry inserts none.
That error happens only if records still fail on the third attempt.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Bulk DML Exception Handling; Triggers and Order of Execution

questions.q: This trigger stamps the date when the stage changes. Updates work, but every new Opportunity fails. Why?
options: Trigger.oldMap is null in insert context, so Trigger.oldMap.get() throws a NullPointerException; check Trigger.isUpdate first
A null old record makes the comparison true, so the stamp is set on every insert
The trigger doesn't compile, because oldMap can't be used in a trigger that includes before insert
o.Id is null in before insert, so the loop skips the record and a required field stays blank
questions.explain: Trigger.old and Trigger.oldMap exist only in update and delete triggers. Calling get() on the null map throws a NullPointerException on insert.
wrong: The code never gets that far: calling get() on a null map throws first.
It compiles; the error happens at run time on insert.
The loop still runs; the failure is the null oldMap.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Trigger Context Variables

questions.q: A sign-up form batch inserts 50 Contacts with Database.insert(contacts, false). Four have '@test.invalid' emails. Which two statements are true? (Choose 2)
options: The SaveResult for each blocked Contact has isSuccess() = false and the message 'Use a real email address.'
The 46 valid Contacts are saved
Database.insert throws a DmlException after the first blocked Contact
All 50 Contacts roll back, because addError in a trigger fails the whole DML call
The 4 blocked Contacts are saved with Email cleared
questions.explain: addError marks just those records as failed. With allOrNone = false, the other records are saved and each failure is reported in its SaveResult.
wrong: With allOrNone = false, errors come back in SaveResults instead of an exception.
Only the records marked with addError fail when partial success is allowed.
Records with addError aren't saved.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Bulk DML Exception Handling; Trigger Context Variables

questions.q: An Apex REST endpoint inserts 150 Cases in one insert statement. What happens with this trigger?
options: It uses 1 SOQL query, because the platform combines identical queries in a loop
It succeeds, because Apex REST requests get the asynchronous limit of 200 queries
It succeeds, but Tasks are created only for the first 100 Cases
The insert fails with a LimitException on the 101st query, and none of the 150 Cases are saved
questions.explain: The query runs once per Case, so the 101st query breaks the synchronous limit of 100. Limit exceptions can't be caught, so the whole transaction rolls back.
wrong: Apex doesn't merge queries; each loop pass runs a query.
Apex REST runs with synchronous limits.
A limit exception rolls back everything; nothing is partly saved.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Execution Governors and Limits

questions.q: This onboarding code retries after a failed Contact insert. What happens at the second insert of a?
options: It inserts the Account named 'Globex (retry)'
It fails, because a still holds the Id from the rolled-back insert; create a new Account (or clone it without the Id)
Database.rollback(sp) throws, because the savepoint was set before the Account insert
It creates a second Account, so the org ends with two Globex records
questions.explain: A rollback doesn't clear the Id on an sObject inserted after the savepoint. Inserting it again fails because the variable has an Id.
wrong: The variable still has an Id, so insert fails.
Rolling back to a savepoint set earlier is the normal use.
The first insert was rolled back and the second fails, so no Account remains.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Transaction Control

questions.q: Importer.run() is called once with 150 Leads in a new transaction. Afterwards, how many DML statements have been used, and what is Importer.attempts?
options: 1 DML statement; attempts = 0
1 DML statement; attempts = 1
3 DML statements; attempts = 1
3 DML statements; attempts = 0
questions.explain: setSavepoint(), insert and rollback() each count against the DML statement limit. Static variables aren't reverted by a rollback, so attempts stays 1.
wrong: Savepoints and rollbacks count as DML statements, and static variables aren't rolled back.
setSavepoint() and rollback() also count as DML statements.
Static variables keep their values after a rollback.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Transaction Control

questions.q: In API version 62.0, this method rolls back a failed order and then sends a failure notice to the ERP with an HTTP callout. The callout throws a CalloutException. What should the developer change?
options: Call Database.releaseSavepoint(sp) after the rollback and before the callout
Nothing; rolling back removes the pending DML, so the callout should work, and the error means the endpoint is down
Move the callout to an @future method, because savepoints and callouts can never share a transaction
Call Database.releaseSavepoint(sp) before Database.rollback(sp)
questions.explain: Since API 60.0, a callout is allowed after a rollback only once all active savepoints are released ('All active Savepoints must be released before making callouts').
wrong: An active savepoint still blocks the callout, even with no pending DML.
They can share a transaction once the savepoint is rolled back and released.
Rolling back after a release throws an error, and the insert would still be pending.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Transaction Control

questions.q: A data import logs failures to Import_Error__c. Support says the Record_Id__c column is always blank, so they can't tell which source rows failed. What is the bug and the fix?
options: getErrors() is empty for failed records; call getMessage() on the SaveResult directly
SaveResults come back in random order; sort them by Id before logging
Database.insert(rows, false) throws on the first failure, so the loop only logs successes
getId() returns null when an insert fails; loop by index and use rows[i] (for example its external key) to identify the row
questions.explain: SaveResults are returned in the same order as the input list, and getId() is null for a failed insert. Use the index to find the source record.
wrong: Failed SaveResults do hold their errors in getErrors().
Results are in the same order as the input list, which is why the index works.
With allOrNone = false, failures are returned, not thrown.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: SaveResult Class

questions.q: A Queueable syncs Account names to a marketing tool. It is enqueued from a button. What happens when the job runs?
options: It sends the names that were cached when the job was enqueued
It throws a NullPointerException, because transient member variables are null when a Queueable runs
It doesn't compile, because transient isn't allowed in classes that implement Queueable
It sends the names, but they may be stale because the cache isn't refreshed
questions.explain: Queueable jobs are serialized when enqueued. Transient variables are skipped and set to null, so cache.get(i) fails in execute().
wrong: Transient variables aren't serialized, so the cache is gone.
transient compiles fine; it just isn't serialized.
The cache is null, not stale.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Queueable Apex

questions.q: A batch job runs with the default scope of 200. For each record it enqueues a Queueable to call a partner API. What happens in the first execute()?
options: 200 Queueable jobs are queued and run in parallel
Up to 50 jobs are queued, then a LimitException is thrown
The second System.enqueueJob call throws a LimitException, because an asynchronous context can add only one Queueable job
The jobs are queued but held until the batch's finish() method completes
questions.explain: Batch execute() runs with asynchronous limits, where System.enqueueJob can be called only once. Collect the Ids and enqueue one job for the whole chunk.
wrong: Only one job can be enqueued from an asynchronous transaction.
50 is the synchronous limit; batch execute() is asynchronous.
Enqueued jobs aren't held for finish(); the second enqueue fails anyway.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Queueable Apex; Execution Governors and Limits

questions.q: An order page enqueues an ERP sync with these options. A user clicks Sync twice, in two separate transactions, while the first job is still waiting in the queue. Which two statements are true? (Choose 2)
options: Both jobs run, with the second starting 2 minutes after the first
In an Apex test, Test.stopTest() waits 2 real minutes before running the job
The second enqueue throws a DuplicateMessageException
The job waits at least 2 minutes before it can start
The signature uses only the class name, so orderId is ignored
questions.explain: Enqueuing a job whose signature matches an already enqueued job throws a DuplicateMessageException. MinimumQueueableDelayInMinutes sets a minimum delay (0-10 minutes); it is ignored in Apex tests.
wrong: A duplicate signature stops the second job from being enqueued at all.
The delay is ignored during Apex tests.
The signature is built from what you add: here the order Id and a string.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Queueable Apex; Apex Reference Guide: QueueableDuplicateSignature.Builder Class

questions.q: This Queueable hits the CPU time limit after processing 120 rows. What does the Job_Log__c record show?
options: Count__c = 120 and Result__c = 'UNHANDLED_EXCEPTION'
Count__c = 0, because the finalizer's state is captured when it is attached
No log is created, because a limit exception also stops the finalizer
Count__c = 120 and Result__c = 'SUCCESS', because the finalizer handles the exception
questions.explain: The finalizer uses its state as it is at the end of the Queueable's execution, so changes after attaching are kept. It runs in its own transaction, so its insert commits even though the job's own DML rolls back.
wrong: Changing the finalizer after it is attached is supported; its state at the end of the job is used.
The finalizer runs in a separate transaction, even after an uncatchable limit exception.
getResult() reports UNHANDLED_EXCEPTION; the finalizer doesn't change the job's result.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Transaction Finalizers

questions.q: A team is adding a Transaction Finalizer to a Queueable that posts invoices. Which two statements about finalizers are true? (Choose 2)
options: A finalizer can enqueue one asynchronous job (Queueable, future or batch)
The finalizer runs in the same transaction as the Queueable, so it can roll back the Queueable's DML
Calling System.attachFinalizer twice attaches two finalizers that both run
Each finalizer run counts as an extra execution against the daily async Apex limit
A finalizer can make callouts
questions.explain: Finalizers run in their own transaction after the Queueable, may make callouts, and may enqueue a single async job.
wrong: The Queueable and its finalizer run in separate transactions.
Only one finalizer can be attached to a Queueable job.
Using a finalizer doesn't count as an extra async execution.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Transaction Finalizers

questions.q: This batch runs over 1,000 records with a scope of 200. Each chunk has 3 failed deletes. What does finish() log?
questions.explain: Database.Stateful keeps instance variables between chunks, so processed reaches 1,000. Static variables aren't kept between batch transactions, so errors is back to 0 in finish().
wrong: Static variables reset in each batch transaction, even with Database.Stateful.
Database.Stateful keeps the instance variable across all 5 chunks.
The instance variable is kept because the class implements Database.Stateful.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Use Batch Apex

questions.q: A batch's start() returns a QueryLocator that finds 9,000 records. It is started with the line below. How many times does execute() run?
questions.code: Id jobId = Database.executeBatch(new ArchiveOrdersBatch(), 5000);
options: None: a LimitException is thrown because the scope is above 2,000
questions.explain: With a QueryLocator, the scope can be at most 2,000. A higher value is reduced, so the records are processed in chunks of up to 2,000: four of 2,000 and one of 1,000.
wrong: A scope above 2,000 isn't used as is with a QueryLocator.
45 would be the default scope of 200, but a scope was passed.
No error is thrown; Salesforce chunks the records into batches of up to 2,000.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Use Batch Apex

questions.q: This batch marks Shipments as sent and posts each one to a carrier API. Every execute() fails with 'You have uncommitted work pending'. What is the fix?
options: Add Database.AllowsCallouts to the class definition
Call an @future(callout=true) method for each record from execute()
Make all the callouts first, then run the update on the scope at the end of execute()
Raise the scope to 2,000 so fewer transactions make callouts
questions.explain: A callout can't follow uncommitted DML in the same transaction. Callouts first, then DML, works in each execute() transaction.
wrong: The class already implements Database.AllowsCallouts; the problem is the order.
Future methods can't be called from Batch Apex.
A bigger scope doesn't change the order, and 2,000 callouts would also pass the 100-callout limit.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Callout Limits and Limitations; Use Batch Apex

questions.q: This scheduled class runs nightly, but the callout fails. Which two changes let the nightly price sync reach the ERP? (Choose 2)
options: Add Database.AllowsCallouts to the Schedulable class
From execute(), enqueue a Queueable that implements Database.AllowsCallouts and makes the callout
From execute(), call a static @future(callout=true) method that makes the callout
Wrap http.send() in try/catch to handle the CalloutException
Return a Continuation from execute()
questions.explain: Synchronous callouts aren't supported from scheduled Apex. Hand the callout to async code that allows callouts, such as a Queueable with Database.AllowsCallouts or a future method with callout=true.
wrong: Database.AllowsCallouts works for Queueable and Batch Apex, not on a Schedulable class.
Catching the exception doesn't make the callout work.
Continuations are for Lightning and Visualforce controllers, not scheduled jobs.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Apex Scheduler

questions.q: A nightly batch sometimes fails a chunk with an uncatchable limit exception. Operations needs the Ids of the records in each failed chunk saved, so they can be retried the next night. What should the developer do?
options: Implement Database.RaisesPlatformEvents on the batch, and subscribe a trigger to BatchApexErrorEvent that saves the JobScope Ids
Wrap the execute() body in try/catch for LimitException and save the scope Ids in the catch block
Implement Database.Stateful, add failed Ids to a list in execute(), and save them in finish()
Attach a Transaction Finalizer in execute() to save the Ids of the chunk if it fails
questions.explain: With Database.RaisesPlatformEvents, an unhandled exception in a batch publishes a BatchApexErrorEvent that includes the failed chunk's record Ids in JobScope.
wrong: Limit exceptions can't be caught.
The failing chunk dies before it can record anything, so its state change is lost.
Transaction Finalizers are only for Queueable jobs.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Use Batch Apex

questions.q: Order_Placed__e is set to Publish After Commit. Audit_Log__e is set to Publish Immediately. chargeCard() throws an exception that nothing catches. What reaches subscribers?
options: Both events, because EventBus.publish isn't affected by rollbacks
Neither event, because events are always discarded when the transaction fails
Only the Order_Placed__e event, because it was published first
Only the Audit_Log__e event; the Order and the Order_Placed__e event are both rolled back
questions.explain: Publish Immediately events go out when the publish call runs, even if the transaction later fails. Publish After Commit events go out only if the transaction commits.
wrong: Publish After Commit events are dropped when the transaction fails.
Publish Immediately events are sent no matter what happens to the transaction.
Publish order doesn't matter; the transaction failed, so the after-commit event is never published.
questions.source: Platform Events Developer Guide: Platform Event Fields; Publish Event Messages with Apex

questions.q: A developer marks a record as 'Sent' when the publish result is successful. A reviewer says isSuccess() doesn't mean what the developer thinks. What does it mean, and how can the code learn the final result?
options: All subscribers received and processed the event; no further check is needed
The publish request was queued (OPERATION_ENQUEUED); pass a publish callback (EventBus.EventPublishFailureCallback or EventPublishSuccessCallback) to EventBus.publish
The subscriber trigger finished without errors; query EventBusSubscriber to confirm
The event was committed with the transaction; check Limits.getDMLStatements() for the final result
questions.explain: Publishing is asynchronous: a successful SaveResult only means the publish was queued. The final publish result arrives in an Apex publish callback.
wrong: isSuccess() says nothing about delivery or processing by subscribers.
The publisher can't know when a subscriber trigger finishes from this result.
A DML counter can't show whether an event was published.
questions.source: Platform Events Developer Guide: Publish Event Messages with Apex; Get the Result of Asynchronous Platform Event Publishing with Apex Publish Callbacks

questions.q: This platform event trigger receives a batch of 1,000 events. Event number 301 has a bad value, and the trigger throws an uncaught exception there. The trigger doesn't use setResumeCheckpoint or RetryableException. What happens?
options: All logs are rolled back, and the whole batch is retried automatically up to 9 times
The logs for the first 300 events stay committed, and the trigger fires again starting at event 301
The logs for the first 300 events stay committed, and the remaining events in that batch aren't processed by this trigger
All logs are rolled back, and the trigger moves straight to the error state
questions.explain: After an uncaught exception, the trigger stops and doesn't process the rest of the batch, but DML done before the exception is committed. Use setResumeCheckpoint to pick up from the last good event.
wrong: Automatic retries happen only when the trigger throws EventBus.RetryableException.
Resuming at the next event needs setResumeCheckpoint.
DML isn't rolled back for an uncaught exception, and the error state follows too many retries, not one exception.
questions.source: Platform Events Developer Guide: Subscribe to Platform Event Notifications with Apex Triggers

questions.q: Payment events sometimes arrive before the ERP has created the matching Invoice__c records, so the trigger below retries. Which two statements about this trigger are true? (Choose 2)
options: When RetryableException is thrown, DML done earlier in that trigger run is rolled back
Only the events after the one that failed are sent again
Without the retries check, the platform would keep retrying forever
On retry, every event in the batch is sent again, in the original ReplayId order
Retried batches always have exactly the same events and size as the first one
questions.explain: Throwing EventBus.RetryableException rolls back the trigger's DML and resends the whole batch in ReplayId order. The trigger can be retried 9 times; after that it moves to the error state.
wrong: That's how setResumeCheckpoint works; a retry resends the whole batch.
After 9 retries the trigger moves to the error state and stops.
Resent batches can be bigger, because new events can be added.
questions.source: Platform Events Developer Guide: Retry Event Triggers with EventBus.RetryableException

questions.q: When an Opportunity is Closed Won, a legacy middleware must receive the Opportunity Id and Amount. It can only accept SOAP messages pushed to its HTTPS endpoint, it is sometimes down for a few hours, and the admin wants no Apex. What should the team use?
options: An outbound message action that sends the fields to the middleware endpoint
Change Data Capture on Opportunity, with the middleware subscribing to the change channel
A custom platform event published by a flow, with an Apex trigger that makes the callout
An Apex REST service that the middleware calls every hour
questions.explain: Outbound messages push a SOAP message with selected fields to an endpoint, need no code, and are retried automatically while the endpoint is down.
wrong: CDC needs the middleware to subscribe as a client (CometD or Pub/Sub API); it doesn't push SOAP to an endpoint.
This needs Apex, and platform event triggers generally can't make callouts directly.
That needs Apex and polling, and the middleware can only receive pushed messages.
questions.source: Salesforce Help: Outbound Messaging; Change Data Capture Developer Guide

questions.q: A shipping partner's API returns HTTP 503 with an HTML maintenance page during upgrades. What happens in this code?
options: Http.send() throws a CalloutException for the 503, so the catch block sets the status to Failed
Http.send() returns null for a 503, so res.getBody() throws a NullPointerException
The platform retries the callout up to 3 times before returning the 503
Http.send() returns normally, then parsing the HTML throws a JSONException that isn't caught; check res.getStatusCode() before parsing
questions.explain: HTTP error codes don't throw in Apex; send() returns the response. Check getStatusCode() first, and only parse the body for a success code.
wrong: CalloutException covers things like timeouts and connection failures, not HTTP error codes.
send() returns an HttpResponse for any HTTP status.
Apex doesn't retry callouts automatically.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: HTTP Classes; Apex Reference Guide: HttpResponse Class

questions.q: A Lightning controller logs an audit entry asynchronously and then calls a credit check service. No DML runs in the method. The callout throws an exception. Why?
options: Future methods run before the rest of the method, so the audit DML is pending when the callout runs
Queuing a future method counts as pending work, so the callout fails with 'You have uncommitted work pending'; make the callout first
A controller can't make a callout and queue async work in the same request; split them into two Lightning calls
A future method and a callout in one transaction exceed the callout limit
questions.explain: Pending operations include DML, queued asynchronous Apex (such as future methods), scheduled Apex and sending email. Do the callout before any of these.
wrong: Future methods run after the transaction commits, not before the callout.
Both are allowed in one request if the callout comes first.
One callout is far below the limit of 100; this is about order.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Callout Limits and Limitations

questions.q: A method calls two endpoints: a token service, then a quotes service. The test below fails because both callouts get the same JSON. Which two changes give each callout its own fake response? (Choose 2)
options: Call Test.setMock twice, once for each endpoint
Use MultiStaticResourceCalloutMock and map each endpoint to its own static resource
Use Test.setMock(WebServiceMock.class, ...) for the second endpoint
Add @IsTest(SeeAllData=true) so the second callout reaches the real service
Write an HttpCalloutMock class whose respond() method returns a different response based on req.getEndpoint()
questions.explain: MultiStaticResourceCalloutMock maps endpoints to static resources, and a custom HttpCalloutMock can branch on the request endpoint.
wrong: The last setMock call replaces the earlier one; it doesn't map mocks to endpoints.
WebServiceMock is for WSDL-based SOAP callouts, not HttpRequest.
Tests can't make real callouts, whatever SeeAllData is set to.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing HTTP Callouts Using Static Resources; Testing HTTP Callouts by Implementing the HttpCalloutMock Interface

questions.q: A partner POSTs JSON orders to /services/apexrest/orders. The contract says: 201 with a JSON body on success, and 422 with a JSON error message when validation fails. Which design meets it?
options: A global static String @HttpPost method that returns '201' or '422' as its result
An @HttpPost method that throws a custom exception for validation failures, so the platform answers with 422
A global static void @HttpPost method that parses RestContext.request.requestBody, sets RestContext.response.statusCode to 201 or 422, and writes RestContext.response.responseBody
A global static Id @HttpPost method that inserts the order and returns its Id, so the platform answers with 201
questions.explain: To control the status code and body, set them on RestContext.response. With no parameters, the raw request body is in RestContext.request.requestBody.
wrong: The returned string becomes the body; the status stays 200.
An unhandled exception returns 400 or 500, never 422.
The platform doesn't switch to 201 for you; to send 201 you set RestContext.response.statusCode yourself.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Apex REST Methods

questions.q: A developer writes this Apex REST resource for a mobile app. It doesn't compile. Which two problems must be fixed? (Choose 2)
options: urlMapping must start with /services/apexrest
Apex REST methods can't return List<Account>
A class can't have two methods annotated with the same HTTP method (@HttpGet)
A @RestResource class can't be declared with sharing
@HttpGet methods can't have parameters; read the name from RestContext.request.params instead
questions.explain: Only one method per HTTP verb is allowed in a @RestResource class, and GET and DELETE methods take no parameters because those requests have no body.
wrong: urlMapping is relative to /services/apexrest; you don't include that prefix.
Lists of sObjects are supported return types.
with sharing is allowed and common on REST resources.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Apex REST Methods

questions.q: A web form posts this JSON to the Apex REST method below: {"email": "ana@example.com", "source": "web"}. The request fails. Which two statements are true? (Choose 2)
options: The JSON must wrap the object in a key named after the parameter: {"customer": {...}}
CustomerDto must implement Serializable to be used as a parameter
Even with the wrapper, source is null, because transient members aren't deserialized
The keys in the JSON must appear in the same order as the class's members
Only global members are deserialized, so a private member would always stay null
questions.explain: Apex REST maps top-level JSON keys to parameter names, so the body needs a 'customer' key. Members marked static or transient aren't deserialized.
wrong: There's no Serializable interface requirement for Apex REST.
Parameter names matter, but their order doesn't.
Public, private and global members are all deserialized.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Apex REST Methods

questions.q: An insurance partner needs a SOAP API to file claims. This class doesn't compile. Which two members cause the errors? (Choose 2)
options: The webservice member variables in the inner ClaimInput class
The second fileClaim method, because webservice methods can't be overloaded
fileClaim(ClaimInput), because webservice methods can't take user-defined types
lookup(), because webservice methods can't return a Map
The global keyword on the outer class, because webservice classes must be public
questions.explain: Apex doesn't allow two webservice methods with the same name, and Maps (like Sets) can't be webservice parameters or return types.
wrong: webservice member variables in an inner class are how you expose a custom type.
Inner classes with webservice members can be used as parameters.
Classes with webservice methods must be global.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Considerations for Using the webservice Keyword; Overloading Web Service Methods

questions.q: Client__c must show a live count of its Completed Project__c records. Project__c has a lookup (not master-detail) to Client__c, and it can't be converted because some Projects have no Client. Integrations mass-update Projects, and the count must stay right when a Project is deleted or restored from the Recycle Bin. What is the best solution?
options: An Apex trigger on Project__c (after insert, update, delete and undelete) that recalculates the counts with one aggregate query per transaction
A roll-up summary field on Client__c that counts Completed Projects
A record-triggered flow on Project__c that runs when a record is created, updated or deleted
A formula field on Client__c that counts the related Projects
questions.explain: Roll-up summary fields need a master-detail relationship, and record-triggered flows have no undelete trigger. A bulkified Apex trigger that handles undelete covers every case.
wrong: Roll-up summary fields aren't available on a lookup relationship.
Record-triggered flows can't run on undelete, so restored Projects wouldn't be counted.
Formula fields can't count child records.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Triggers; Salesforce Help: Roll-Up Summary Field; Salesforce Help: Record-Triggered Flows

questions.q: A record-triggered flow on Account calls this action to get a credit score. In bulk loads, some Accounts get another Account's score. What is wrong?
options: Invocable methods can't run SOQL; pass the scores in from the flow instead
The method must be global to run in bulk
The flow calls the action once per record, so the List always holds one Id and the bug is elsewhere
The outputs must match the inputs in size and order; build the result by looping over accountIds and looking each one up in a Map
questions.explain: Flow bulkifies interviews into one call, and the i-th output must belong to the i-th input. Skipping Accounts with no score shifts every later result.
wrong: Invocable methods can run SOQL; that's how they get the scores.
public is enough for an invocable method; global isn't needed.
Flow batches interviews and passes many Ids in one call.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: InvocableMethod Annotation
